why: Careless responding is common in online questionnaires and quietly ruins profiles. Combine direct checks (infrequency and instructed items) with indirect ones (response time, long strings, consistency).

infrequency_items.note: Same response scale as the surrounding block. The keyed answer is 1 or 2 ('inaccurate'). Original items; keep them mildly plausible in tone so they don't feel like traps.

items.text: Have never used a phone or a computer.
Sleep less than one hour every night.
Have visited every country in the world.
Can run 100 metres in under three seconds.

instructed_items.note: Use sparingly; more than one per ~50 items irritates people.

items.text: To show you are reading carefully, choose 'Moderately inaccurate' for this statement.

self_report_effort.text: Be honest, it won't count against you: should we use your answers from this session to build your profile?
options: No, I wasn't really paying attention
self_report_effort.action: 'Partly' -> offer to redo the rushed block. 'No' -> discard the session and ask them to retake it later.

indirect_indices.page_time: Flag a block if median response time < 1.0 s per Likert item (likely not reading).
indirect_indices.longstring: Flag if the same option is chosen > 12 times in a row in any Likert block.
indirect_indices.even_odd_consistency: Split each multi-item scale into even and odd items, correlate halves across scales; flag if r < .30.
indirect_indices.psychometric_antonyms: Use the 27 opposite-content IPIP-NEO pairs (file 01). Flag if the within-person correlation across pairs is > -.10.
indirect_indices.cognitive_rt: On ability items, flag responses < 25% of the item's median time from the norm sample (rapid guessing). Score those items as missing, not wrong.

decision_rule: Two or more flags in a session -> mark the session 'low confidence', show the user why, and offer a retake. Never silently discard data and never shame the user.
